questions.question: In $\ell(t)=A+tv$, what does the point $A$ provide?
options: A specific point on the line.
A normal vector to the line.

questions.question: In $\ell(t)=A+tv$, what does the vector $v$ provide?
options: A second fixed point at which the line must end.
The normal vector of a plane.

questions.question: What set of parameter values is used for a full line?
Why can the same line have many parametric representations?
options: Changing representation changes a line into a plane.
The parameter must always be renamed.
Base points can shift and direction vectors can be rescaled.
A line has no fixed points.

questions.question: How can one test whether a point lies on a parametrised line?
options: Check whether it equals $A+tv$ for some real $t$.
Check whether it is orthogonal to $A$.
Check only whether its first coordinate equals $t$.

questions.question: For $\ell(t)=(4+t,2+t)$, what is a direction vector?
For $\ell(t)=(4+t,2+t)$, what point is obtained at $t=0$?
Which parametrisation describes the line through $(1,0)$ in direction $(2,3)$?
Does $(3,3)$ lie on $\ell(t)=(1,1)+t(2,2)$?
options: No, because the starting point is different.
No, because $(3,3)$ is not a direction vector.

questions.question: Why does $\ell(t)=x+t(y-x)$ pass through both $x$ and $y$?
options: At $t=0$ it gives $x$, and at $t=1$ it gives $y$.
At every $t$ it gives both points at once.

questions.question: For $\ell(t)=A+tv$ with $v\ne0$, which parameter set traces the full line?
Why must the direction vector in a useful line parametrisation be nonzero?
options: A zero direction would give only the single point $A$.
A zero direction gives every point in the space.
A zero direction gives a plane.
A zero direction is the only direction that defines a line.

questions.question: Find a parametrisation of the line through $x=(1,2)$ and $y=(4,8)$.
For $\ell(t)=(2-t,1+3t)$, which direction vector matches the parametrisation?
For which $t$ does $\ell(t)=(1,2)+t(2,1)$ give $(5,4)$?
Why do $A+tv$ and $A+s(2v)$ describe the same line when $v\ne0$?
options: Changing from $t$ to $s$ only rescales the parameter.
The second parametrisation contains only half the line.
They have different starting points, so they cannot agree.

questions.question: If a point satisfies the first coordinate equation of $A+tv$, why might it still fail to lie on the line?
options: Only one coordinate equation is ever needed.
The parameter may be chosen separately for each coordinate.
The direction vector disappears after one coordinate is checked.
The same parameter must satisfy all coordinate equations.

questions.question: Does $(3,5,7)$ lie on $\ell(t)=(1,1,1)+t(1,2,3)$?
options: No, because the direction vector is not a unit vector.
No, because the coordinates are unequal.

questions.question: Does $(2,4)$ lie on $\ell(t)=(1,1)+t(1,2)$?
options: No, because $(1,2)$ is not a valid direction vector.
No; the coordinate equations give different values of $t$.
